## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track people gate, wave People. No audit backlog id. Created from the audit's rulings and blueprint, not from a backlog line (see Findings).

Persona and route: Sessions on the Azure dev app after the redeploy, with the concept open beside it. Synthetic patients only.
Findings and reviewers: All findings marked as needing clinical validation; the 21 decisions of the validation plan. No UX number in the backlog: the plan itself is the source.
Rationale: No clinician, nurse, receptionist or owner took part in the audit. Nothing safety-sensitive should be built from the audit alone, and twelve tickets may not merge until a named person has agreed.
Proposed UX behaviour: The founder runs the four scripted sessions of the plan (doctor 40 minutes on the room device, receptionist 30 at the desk, nurse 20 on a tablet, owner 20) and records each of the 21 decisions with the person's role and the date, on the ticket that the decision blocks. Rows 1 to 5 come first, before the first safety tickets merge. The founder also collects the doctor's list of about 100 medicines with brands, fixes the training date and says whether screens may change shape before it or only after the first pilot weeks, and checks on site which devices are used at the desk, in the room and by the nurse (mouse or touch), including one run of the consultation and nurse intake on a real tablet.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html and docs/product-ux-audit/12-prototype-guide.md (What to try).
Components and tokens affected: None.
Front end and back end split: People only. No code.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the Azure redeploy ticket (the sessions run on the redeployed app) and by the signed pilot agreement (MDV-P1-043).
Clinical sign-off: This ticket is the sign-off. It stands apart from the clinical advisor's journey sign-off (MDV-P1-073), which is still required.
Effort and regression risk: M (calendar time, not build time) · None to the code. Schedule risk: every ticket that names a question waits for it.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) A clinical safety standard: the plan's criteria are the audit's proposals. (2) Real patient data in any session. (3) The journey sign-off of MDV-P1-073.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given the validation plan, when the first safety tickets are ready to merge, then decisions 1 to 5 are recorded with role and date on the tickets they block
- [ ] **AC2.** Given the plan's table, when this gate closes, then each of the 21 rows has an answer, a name by role and a date, on the blocked ticket and summarised here
- [ ] **AC3.** Given the doctor's session on the changed consultation, when asked whose record is this and what is she allergic to without scrolling, then the answer is right three times out of three
- [ ] **AC4.** Given the doctor's session, when the usual antibiotic is prescribed for the penicillin-allergic synthetic patient, then no medicine of that class is authorised without a stop the doctor noticed
- [ ] **AC5.** Given the receptionist's session, when she presses Call in on the wrong patient, then she recovers without help
- [ ] **AC6.** Given this gate, when it closes, then the brand list is attached to the brand ticket, the training date is written on the navigation names ticket and the device check is written here
- [ ] **AC7.** Given every session, when notes and screenshots are stored, then they hold synthetic patients only and no real person's health data

## Test notes

- No automated test. The scenario scripts of the plan (section 2) are the procedure; the questions of section 3 are asked after each session.

## Notes / open questions
